verdict: Run against measured Perturb-seq (on knockouts that actually DO something — >=25 moved genes each), the fieldsim engine's forward prediction is at CHANCE: it ranks which genes move at AUC 0.5 (random 0.5), and — the decisive comparison — that is no better than the STATIC baseline of just listing the knockout's curated targets with no dynamics (AUC 0.499). So the Hill+decay+diffusion machinery adds nothing over the network topology it was handed. The mechanism is coverage: fieldsim can only touch genes on a curated regulatory path from the knockout, so it reaches only ~3% of the genes that actually moved while lighting up a ~499-gene neighborhood that mostly did NOT move — huge false reach, near-zero recall. And on the few movers it does reach, direction is if anything WORSE than a coin-flip (pooled sign agreement 0.156, below 0.5 on n=32) — the propagated curated regulatory signs actively disagree with the measured response, consistent with the earlier finding that curated regulation recovers the measured knockout at ~chance. This is the same far-field-does-not-compose wall every engine here hit (transitivity ~0.009). CONCLUSION: fieldsim is a correct, internally-consistent MECHANISTIC DEMONSTRATOR whose forward prediction of a real knockout does NOT beat chance or a trivial network lookup. The measured `knockout`/`cascade` engines — which report what was observed and honestly flag the ~84% they can't route — remain the trustworthy tools.
